anatomy.intro: The numbered illustration explains a living Mammillaria bombycina reference; it is a botanical guide, not a measured portrait.

parts.function: Fine covering between the tubercles helps create the silky appearance.
parts.label: White wool

parts.function: Pale spreading spokes surround each spine-bearing areole.
parts.label: Radial spines

parts.function: A stronger reddish-brown hook projects through the white covering.
parts.label: Hooked central spine

parts.function: A young side head can develop into another cylinder within the clump.
parts.label: Basal offset

flowers.text: Living M. bombycina can produce deep rose-pink flowers about 1.5 cm across. The bright flowers stand out against the white coat, but no flowering claim is made for the former collection plant.

growth.note: These are species life stages; the historical collection plant was removed and has no retained living offset.

stages.text: A living juvenile begins as a small spiny globe.
stages.title: Young head

stages.text: The stem lengthens and develops a dense pale coat.
stages.title: Longer cylinder

stages.text: Offsets can gather into a spreading group.
stages.title: Cluster of heads

habitat.text: Mammillaria bombycina is native to southwestern Aguascalientes and northeastern Jalisco, Mexico, in dry shrubland. The illustrated plant represents that species, not a surviving collection specimen. The former collection plant was a probable identification from older photographs and remains a historical record after its removal on July 24, 2026.

A living botanical reference of Mammillaria bombycina: cluster of three short cylindrical green cactus stems covered in dense white radial spines and white wool between tubercles, with reddish-brown central spines with hooked tips. 1 points to white axillary wool between tubercles, 2 to a pale radial spine cluster at an areole, 3 to a reddish-brown hooked central spine, 4 to a small basal offset. lookalikes.name: Mammillaria cf. rekoi
lookalikes.text: Both may have hooked central spines; the rekoi candidate has more exposed green tissue and a less heavily woolled appearance.

mature.text: RHS describes clustering cylindrical stems reaching about 20 cm. The width of a whole clump depends on its offset count, so a single stem's height does not describe the entire colony.

milestones.text: Final inspection found only a tiny surviving green patch; no offset was retained. The page preserves the plant's history.
milestones.title: Removed from the collection

nameStory.text: Kew records the species name as first published by Quehl in 1910.
